[h2]Resumen del Juego[/h2]
TRON RUN/r es ese híbrido de [b]acción + carreras[/b] donde tu trabajo consiste en correr como si te persiguiera la factura de la luz… pero en neón. Es un arcade de reflejos y rutas: parkour futurista, esquivas milimétricas, saltos, paredes y la sensación constante de que el juego te odia (y tú lo agradeces… a ratos).

La primera impresión es clara: [b]minimalismo cyberpunk[/b], velocidad y “una más y me voy”. No esperes una campaña narrativa épica: esto va de dominar circuitos, memorizar patrones y dejar tu dignidad en el piso cuando el obstáculo que “ya tenías controlado” te vuelve a borrar del mapa.

Lo No Tan Bueno:

TRON RUN/r is a fast, demanding, and stylish arcade experience developed by Sanzaru Games Inc. and published by Disney that reinterprets the TRON universe through the lens of high-speed reflex gameplay. Rather than focusing on exploration or narrative-driven progression, the game is built entirely around momentum, precision, and mastery, positioning itself as a skill-based runner that values repetition and improvement. From the moment it begins, TRON RUN/r establishes an uncompromising tone: success is earned through muscle memory, sharp reactions, and an understanding of its layered movement systems, not through casual experimentation.

At its core, the game revolves around sprinting through neon-soaked circuits while avoiding hazards, defeating enemies, and maintaining speed. The primary on-foot mode emphasizes parkour-like traversal, combining jumps, slides, wall runs, rail grinding, and disc combat into a single flowing system. Levels are carefully designed obstacle courses rather than randomly generated tracks, which gives each run a sense of structure and intentional challenge. Mastery comes from learning layouts, anticipating hazards, and chaining movements together efficiently, creating a rhythm that feels closer to a precision platformer than a traditional endless runner.

Combat is integrated seamlessly into movement rather than existing as a separate system. Enemies and destructible barriers are placed directly along traversal paths, requiring players to attack without breaking momentum. The identity disc functions as both a weapon and a tool for clearing paths, adding an extra layer of decision-making at high speed. Poor timing can easily lead to collisions or lost flow, reinforcing the idea that combat in TRON RUN/r is about precision and timing rather than brute force.

The game expands beyond its core running mode with several distinct gameplay variations. Light cycle levels introduce a different tempo, focusing on drifting, cornering, and threading through narrow gaps at extreme speeds. These sections test spatial awareness and reaction time in a different way, offering variety while maintaining the game’s emphasis on mechanical skill. The inclusion of an endless-style mode further extends replayability, combining elements from multiple modes into a constantly escalating challenge that pushes endurance and consistency to their limits.

Progression is handled through a system of unlocks and upgrades that reward repeated play rather than narrative advancement. Completing challenges earns currency that can be spent on new characters, visual variations, companions, and gameplay modifiers. While these upgrades provide subtle advantages or cosmetic variety, they never override the importance of skill. The game remains fundamentally demanding regardless of unlocks, ensuring that progression feels like a supplement to mastery rather than a shortcut around difficulty.

Visually, TRON RUN/r fully embraces the aesthetic introduced in TRON: Legacy, filling the screen with glowing lines, sharp geometry, and stark contrasts between light and darkness. The environments are abstract yet readable, designed to ensure clarity even at extreme speeds. This visual clarity is crucial, as the game frequently demands split-second decisions that would be impossible in cluttered environments. The presentation is clean, consistent, and unmistakably TRON, reinforcing immersion through style rather than realism.

The soundtrack plays a major role in shaping the experience. Electronic music drives the pace of each run, reinforcing momentum and heightening intensity as difficulty ramps up. The audio design complements the visuals perfectly, creating a sensory loop where sound, motion, and rhythm align. While individual tracks may not stand out in isolation, their integration into gameplay enhances focus and flow, helping players fall into the game’s demanding cadence.

Difficulty is one of the game’s defining traits and also its most divisive aspect. TRON RUN/r is not forgiving, especially for newcomers. Mistakes are punished quickly, and progress often requires repeated failure and memorization. However, the challenge is largely fair, rooted in consistent rules and readable hazards rather than randomness. For players who enjoy incremental improvement and chasing perfect runs, this difficulty becomes addictive. For others, particularly those seeking a more relaxed arcade experience, it may feel overly punishing.

Overall, TRON RUN/r is a focused and confident arcade title that prioritizes skill, repetition, and style over accessibility or narrative depth. It succeeds by understanding exactly what it wants to be: a high-speed test of reflexes set within one of science fiction’s most visually distinctive worlds. While it may not appeal to casual players or those unfamiliar with demanding action games, it offers a deeply satisfying experience for players willing to commit to mastery. As a TRON game, it captures the essence of speed, precision, and digital danger remarkably well, delivering a neon-lit challenge that rewards dedication and persistence.

Rating: 7/10

This is an electrifying, high-speed celebration of the Grid that remains the definitive way to experience the neon-soaked world of TRON in a fast-paced format. Even now the game continues to stand out for its incredible sense of momentum, flawlessly blending "Runner" and "Cycle" modes with a fluid movement system that makes every wall-run and light-cycle turn feel exhilarating. The visual fidelity is stunning, glowing aesthetic of TRON: Legacy, while the pulsing electronic soundtrack—featuring contributions from EDM legend Giorgio Moroder—drives the action forward with infectious energy.

Beyond its core levels, the "STREAM" mode offers a challenging, procedurally generated gauntlet that provides endless replayability for those looking to dominate the global leaderboards. Although this game is indeed not TRON 2.0, by all means, TRON 2.0 is another level game. However! The game captures the spirit of the franchise perfectly, offering a wide array of character and cycle customizations that allow you to truly inhabit the role of a Program. Whether you are expertly throwing your identity disc to shatter enemies or weaving through data-walls at top speed, TRON RUN/r is a polished, stylish, and incredibly addictive arcade experience that no fan of the series should miss.

When I first saw this game, I thought this was a cheap cash in on a cool IP. I'm glad to report that I was wrong.

I'm a huge fan of both the original TRON as well as the 2000s sequel movie and Cartoon Series. This game nails the aesthetic of both Uprising and Legacy and even expands on it a bit. If you're a fan of auto-runners like temple run or sonic dash, this game takes it a few steps further with decently challenging levels and multiple game-play modes. Disc Running, Light Cycling, and a marathon mode that mixes both previously mentioned modes. The game offers leader boards for every level and even though I am personally not super competitive with this type of game, I can see people using this feature. I can even see the speed-running community taking this game to the limit and perfecting every level.

Even with all the positives, I don't really know if it is worth a full $20. More if you want the extensions. Even though its a good game and a great addition to the Tron franchise, it feels a little light for the price. Not a ton of voice clips or customization options (mainly colors and gender options, as well as a pretty cool inclusion of some OG characters) to make the world fill built out. Base game only has 16 levels per game mode, and the marathon mode is fun but difficult unless you get really good at both modes. I don't know about the extender bundles because I don't own them, but I assume it adds more levels to each mode. If so, I may get them in the future if they're on sale (or if I end up feeling the need for some more TRON).

If this game goes on sale and you like TRON, buy it. If it goes on sale and you like auto-runners, buy it. If you like both TRON AND auto-runners, buy it, even if its not on sale!

Played this game a lot on PS4 and had to get it here as well. In my opinion this is still the best runner game on PC. Great setting, amazing graphics and very smooth/polished gameplay. Special movement like wall running or gliding feels especially good and you can master things like last second evades to increase your highscore. Maybe my favorite thing are the race parts where you drift along the tracks (with drifting controls similar to Sonic Allstar Racing = best), try to find the perfect line and kick your rivals from bikes like in Road Rash.

I wish the endless mode would still have functioning leaderboards/weekly challenges, but at least it's still playable.

I really love Tron and I think for maybe the first few impressions you'll gather from Tron RUN/r will get you in that mood for a while. I don't think though it won't be for long as this game prides itself into being grind heavy, the kind of grinding where it'll dangle the easier option of using actual money to make things easier for you to shave away from the in-game time of grinding. I actually even wondered if this was a mobile port because that's the kind of thing you'd expect from mobile games, since you have a 3-star system here, you have MTX options .etc

But no, this is not the case at all, this appears to have been an experimental release by Disney to see how it'd fare with what we're given here.

The whole premise of the game is that you've got two modes, not counting Endless, where you're on foot and the other you're on the infamous light cycles. You go through 16 levels per mode, collecting bits, throwing your disc at threats, unlock other abilities through the purchase of said bits (or through MTX) all the while doing it in one very linear track. There is no room to explore, it's just do things the best way you can and go through repeats necessary for better results. Rinse and repeat.

And that kind of gameplay in a very inviting digitized world of TRON is kinda saddening, for it to be treated like this. If you are a fan of "runner" type games, this one is very fun!  The runs are a total rush.  However, the game has no plot nor do you "level up" your character.  The only sense of progression is trying to get the max of three gold stars for perfect completion of each level.

Here are some tips for new players: 

1. The "red" power-ups that you can optionally buy before each level (on the left side of the screen) are not "always on."  You must press 'Y' during the run to activate them, and they stay active for several seconds.  They are single-use BUT there are floating purple boxes in the levels which you can hit with your disk to re-charge the power up.  

2. The "data piercing energy" one does excellent damage against tanks.  Also, destroying green data barriers does give points, and data piercing can help burst through thick walls for more points.

3. The blue power-ups, on the right side of the screen, are always-on if you buy one. 

4. The bit-doubler power-up is not good for trying to make runs more profitable.  Its cost negates most of the extra bits gained, since it is not an always-on powerup,  Its primary use is to increase your score so you can get all three stars on hard runs. 

5. If you need to grind for bits, level 3 is an easy runs that rewards high bits and can be completed without any power-ups

I avoided writing a review for TRON RUN/r for quite a while because I couldn't answer one basic question: "Do you recommend this game?"

The truth is, I'm not sure.  If we're talking about going back in time and talking to myself when it first came out, then yes, I would absolutely recommend the game to myself.  If I'm talking to any die-hard TRON fans, or fans of speedruns or other runner games, then yes, I would recommend it.  But I still have the free giftable copy of the game I bought with the Deluxe Edition, and I haven't tried to gift it to any of my friends.  The niche of this game is very small, and it was tainted on release with the smell of "microtransactions" and is tainted now by lack of support.  The short version is that this game is an enjoyable but deeply flawed mess.

Only the most hardcore of TRON fans will enjoy it, because it does virtually nothing with the TRON story.  It's visually beautiful and has the aesthetic that is immediately recognizable as TRON.  But it's all style and no substance.  There is no story in the game, and I don't mean it has a bad story.  I mean there is absolutely no overarching narrative.  The only reference to the overall TRON story is the character skins.  And some gameplay elements are missing that unique "TRON" touch.  The game features light cycles, but you don't build intricate mazes with them to trap your opponent.... you just RUN. 
 Meanwhile, if you're mainly interested in runner games or speedruns, high scores and power-ups could be bought through microtransactions rather than sheer skill.  As a result, the game didn't really find it's target market from a gameplay perspective, and now the leaderboards have been taken down.

But there really is a fun game buried in all these issues.  For players who enjoy games that demand quick-response or that enjoy finding and learning patterns (like all those Rock Band and Guitar Hero games), this is a beautiful, cool game.  Watch any video playthrough on youTube and you will see vibrant colors, a electronic soundtrack fitting for TRON, and a fast-paced and fluid gameplay.  

I wish I had gotten into the game when it first came out.  I wish it had done better at finding a community and didn't shoot itself in the foot with microtransactions.  I wish it had some sort of story to follow, or a place in the TRON franchise.  But as it is, it was fun to throw myself against fast-paced obstacles, tight turns, and neon enemies.  I'm glad I played it, maybe you will be too.

To be clear, I really like this game. It's the best endless runner I've ever played and it's great mechanically and sonically, though as many have stated if you want to get the full experience, turn the game music down to 0 and blast the Tron: Legacy soundtrack. There are three game modes - four if you have the DLC - stage based runner, light cycle, endless runner, and the hybrid of the two. The latter two are definitely the most fun IMO, and I spent most of my 16 hours at the time of review playing DLC maps and the endless mode.

Visually, it's nice at first but it gets stale fast. Even for a $30 game, the world of TRON deserves so much more than what this game gives it. It still looks nice; the characters and tracks are pretty good, but everything surrounding those things are sub-par. The neon lines everywhere are there just for the sake of being there.

I bought the Ultimate Edition, and it is absolutely not worth the price. It's double the price of the base game, which is already too expensive, and only adds some character customisation options and the new hybrid game mode. And yet, without it, the game is too sparse for content.

Also, when it released it had some live content that was keyed to some big features as well as a couple of achievements. There are some really hard challenges that I thought were a blast to complete though, even if I couldn't 100% complete the game.

If you ever spot the Ultimate Edition on sale, I recommend picking it up. It's good fun and if you're a fan of endless runners I can easily imagine it lasting you up to 25 hours. I don't doubt that I'll come back to this game every now and then.

As it is though, being $60 AUD for the full package, with features missing... don't waste your money, unless you're a desperate TRON fan like me.
